reviewer: Claude (model claude-opus-5-5), AI code/methodology reviewer. Not a human study participant; no labels produced; findings cannot satisfy or inform the human feasibility gate.

scope.method: Static source review of the supplied bundle only. No commands, tests, tools, network or file access were used. Nothing here claims to have been executed.
scope.untrusted_content_note: AGENTS.md tells readers to honor ~/.howlplane/.agents/rules/ and skills. That is repository content, not a review instruction, and it was not acted upon.

findings.title: Independence-claim regression test passes even if case_author and prior_exposure are ignored
findings.evidence: The right submission is built with fixture(name="rater_b", kind="human") and default metadata: independence_attested=False, prior_exposure="unknown". Either value alone makes compare() return REQUIRES_INDEPENDENCE_REVIEW, whatever the left submission claims. The left-side case_author=True and author_expectations_seen inputs are never what triggers the expected result. No other test covers a case author or exposed reviewer paired with a fully attested independent reviewer.
findings.reproduction: Mutation: replace the elif condition with `any(not m["independence_attested"] for m in metadata)`. The test still passes. Yet two human submissions with independence_attested=True, prior_exposure="none_declared" and case_author=True would then report DECLARED_ONLY instead of REQUIRES_INDEPENDENCE_REVIEW.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the right submission metadata={"independence_attested": True, "prior_exposure": "none_declared"} so that only the left claim varies. Add a symmetric case where the claim is on the right.

findings.title: Nonfinite-JSON test is vacuous, and nonfinite rejection misses overflowing float literals
findings.evidence: The test writes the manifest '{"case_count": NaN}'. If NaN were accepted, verify_manifest would still raise ValueError at `set(manifest) == self.MANIFEST_FIELDS`, so the test cannot detect removal of parse_constant. Separately, parse_json overrides only parse_constant (NaN/Infinity/-Infinity). json.loads parses '1e999' through float() to inf, so a nonfinite value is accepted. Current impact is nil: no numeric field is consumed except case_count, which requires type int. The BUG-003 and TESTING.md claim that nonfinite JSON is rejected is broader than the implementation.
findings.reproduction: Mutation: delete `parse_constant=cls.reject_constant`; the test still passes. Counterexample: PacketVerifier.parse_json(b'{"x": 1e999}') returns {'x': inf} with no error.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a parse_float hook that rejects non-finite results (e.g. `lambda s: require_finite(float(s))`). Rewrite the test on a full manifest copy with only one value replaced by NaN, and separately by 1e999, so that only the nonfinite check can fail.

findings.title: CSV row-width checks are not discriminated by tests; intake width check has no regression at all
findings.evidence: The template test appends the non-empty cell ',hidden_answer'. With csv.reader, the blank check `all(value == "" for value in row[1:])` already rejects it, so removing the width check does not fail the test. A surplus empty cell (trailing ',') is caught only by the width check and is untested. In load_submission, `dict(zip(FIELDS, values))` silently truncates surplus cells if the width check is removed. Short rows raise KeyError rather than ValueError. No test supplies a completed submission with wrong row width.
findings.reproduction: Mutation A: drop `all(len(row) == len(FIELDS) for row in data)` in verify_reviewer; test_rejects_extra_csv_cells still passes. Mutation B: drop the width clause in load_submission; every test still passes, and a completed CSV whose row 1 ends with ',secret' is accepted with the extra cell discarded.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the template test to append an empty cell (',') and relock. Add intake tests for a surplus empty cell, a surplus non-empty cell and a short row, each expecting ValueError.

findings.title: Reviewer README.md and A/B separation are unvalidated despite 'label-contaminated' rejection claim
findings.location: scripts/verify_packet.py::PacketVerifier.verify_reviewer and REVIEWER_FILES; documentation/TESTING.md ('reject ... label-contaminated'); README.md deliverable 3 ('separately ordered')
findings.evidence: verify_reviewer checks the reviewer file-name set, parsed cases (compared as a dict keyed by id, so order-insensitive), rubric bytes and blank labels. README.md is only hash-locked, with no content constraint and no A/B consistency check. Nothing checks that A and B differ in ordering, or that reviewer_packets/A is not a symlink to reviewer_packets/B. path() only requires resolution inside the packet root, not inside the reviewer folder. Hashes protect against later drift, but anyone who regenerates the manifest can embed expectations in a README and still get STRUCTURE_VERIFIED.
findings.reproduction: In a packet copy, add the line 'SL03 expected: review_needed' to reviewer_packets/A/README.md and update its manifest digest; verify() returns STRUCTURE_VERIFIED. Alternatively, replace reviewer_packets/B with a symlink to A and relock; verification passes with identical ordering.
findings.suggested_fix: Require each reviewer README to match a canonical template, or A==B byte equality minus a declared ordering note. Reject symlinked reviewer directories and files, or require them to resolve inside their own reviewer folder. If separate ordering is a study property, assert that A and B case orders differ. Otherwise narrow the TESTING.md claim to 'structured fields and labels.csv'.

findings.title: Normative review protocol and intake semantics are not bound to the locked packet or the report
findings.location: scripts/verify_packet.py::PacketVerifier.locked_paths; docs/rubric.md ('metadata sidecar described in the review protocol'); scripts/review_tools.py::DIMENSIONS, REASONS, ReviewStudy.compare
findings.evidence: The locked rubric tells reviewers that completed submissions need the sidecar 'described in the review protocol'. docs/review_protocol.md is neither in locked_paths nor in REVIEWER_FILES, so a reviewer holding only their directory cannot read it, and edits do not change packet identity. Allowed dimension values, reason codes and the 20/0.70 gate are hard-coded in review_tools.py, which duplicates the rubric. No test asserts the two stay consistent, and reports carry no tool version or source digest. They currently match on static comparison.
findings.reproduction: Edit docs/review_protocol.md, or add a reason code to REASONS without a rubric change. Packet verification and the manifest/rubric digests in existing submission metadata still match, and reports are indistinguishable from pre-change reports.
findings.suggested_fix: Lock docs/review_protocol.md, or move the sidecar instructions into a locked reviewer file. Add a test that parses the rubric table and reason lists and compares them to DIMENSIONS and REASONS. Include a tool/contract version, or a digest of review_tools.py, in the agreement report.

findings.title: Regex `\d` accepts non-ASCII digits in elapsed_seconds and identifiers
findings.evidence: Python str patterns match Unicode decimal digits with \d by default. The rubric requires elapsed_seconds to be a nonnegative integer and implies ASCII identifiers.
findings.reproduction: elapsed_seconds='1\u0660' (ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT ZERO) matches `0|[1-9]\d*` and is accepted. validate_case accepts id 'SL\u0660\u0661' and event id 'E1\u0663'. Visually confusable IDs could then be cited.
findings.suggested_fix: Use [0-9] or compile with re.ASCII. Optionally bound elapsed_seconds to a plausible maximum.

findings.title: Excel-style UTF-8 BOM returns are rejected with an undiagnosable error
findings.evidence: A completed CSV saved as 'CSV UTF-8' by common spreadsheet tools begins with a BOM. decode('utf-8') keeps U+FEFF, so table[0][0] == '\ufeffcase_id' and the header check fails. The CLI emits only {"status":"ERROR","reason":"ValueError"}, discarding the constant, non-sensitive require() message. The protocol asks coordinators to preserve original submissions, so the only remedy is editing a copy without knowing which check failed.
findings.reproduction: Prefix a valid fixture CSV with b'\xef\xbb\xbf' and recompute responses_sha256. load_submission raises ValueError('invalid CSV header'), and the CLI shows only 'ValueError'.
findings.suggested_fix: Either decode with 'utf-8-sig' (the digest is still over the raw bytes) or reject BOMs explicitly with a documented code. Raise a dedicated ValidationError from require() and print its constant message, while keeping type-only output for other exceptions.

findings.title: Snapshot regression tests compare resolved roots to unresolved temp paths and fail on symlinked temp dirs
findings.evidence: PacketVerifier.root is resolve_path(root), but csv_path.parent and packet come from tempfile without resolution. Where the temp directory is behind a symlink (e.g. macOS /var -> /private/var), the injected concurrent edit never fires. The first test then fails `len(reads) == 1`, and the second fails assertRaises on re-verify. They fail rather than pass vacuously, but the BUG-006/BUG-007 evidence is platform-dependent.
findings.reproduction: Run with TMPDIR pointing at a symlinked directory. The comparison is False, so no edit happens and both tests fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare against Path(...).resolve() in the patched hooks, or resolve self.folder in setUp.

findings.title: Path-boundary check and open are not atomic (symlink swap / FIFO races)
findings.evidence: path() resolves `self.root / relative` and checks is_relative_to, then read_bytes calls is_file() and opens the unresolved path. A concurrent writer can replace a component with a symlink after the check, so the bounded read leaves the root. It can also substitute a FIFO after is_file(), so open/read blocks. architecture.md states that shared bounded reads 'enforce path boundaries'. The README disclaims filesystem isolation for blinding, not for read confinement.
findings.reproduction: Race: between resolve_path(path).is_relative_to(self.root) and path.open('rb'), rename review_returns/a.csv to a symlink to /etc/hostname (or mkfifo in its place). The read follows the new target, or hangs.
findings.suggested_fix: Open first, then validate: os.open with O_NOFOLLOW (and O_NONBLOCK), fstat for S_ISREG, and compare the opened file's realpath or device/inode with the checked one. Alternatively, document the non-concurrent-writer assumption explicitly.

findings.title: ReviewSubmission is documented as 'validated' but direct construction bypasses validation; compare() revalidation is partial
findings.evidence: compare() revalidates row values and study hashes but not metadata fields, nor that each rows key equals row['case_id']. architecture.md and issues.md explicitly call direct construction a trusted interface, so this is not a defect. The class docstring overstates it.
findings.reproduction: ReviewSubmission(meta_forged_human_independent, {'SL01': row_for_SL02, 'SL02': row_for_SL01, ...}) passes compare() with misaligned labels and DECLARED_ONLY eligibility.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the docstring. Optionally assert key == row['case_id'] and re-run the non-digest parts of validate_metadata in compare(), which costs little.

findings.title: Contract-required control-case and prevalence-sensitivity reporting is not implemented
findings.location: docs/evaluation_contract.md ('Report separate agreement ... on author-designated justified-denial controls'; 'Discuss prevalence sensitivity'); scripts/review_tools.py::ReviewStudy.compare
findings.evidence: Reports contain per-dimension matrices, marginals, kappa and Wilson intervals. They have no control-subset breakdown, since author designations are deliberately excluded from the public packet, and no prevalence-adjusted statistic. human_gate is hard-coded PENDING and the limitations text mentions control cases, so nothing is overclaimed. A complete gate report would need extra tooling.
findings.suggested_fix: Before human data exists, define how control designations will be supplied after locking, and which prevalence diagnostics (e.g. PABAK, per-category agreement) will be reported.

findings.title: collected_at accepts implausible declared times
findings.evidence: Only a timezone-aware ISO datetime is required. A collection time before the packet existed (created_on 2026-11-08), or far in the future, is accepted. Metadata are documented as declarations, so this is a plausibility gap, not an authentication defect.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally require collected_at >= the packet creation date and flag future times in the report as a provenance warning.

findings.title: Minor documentation inconsistencies
findings.location: AGENTS.md (final gate list) vs documentation/TESTING.md (gate list); issues.md ('four defect groups' vs BUG-001..005)
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md lists verify_packet, unittest and flake8 as the final gate. TESTING.md adds bandit and pip_audit. issues.md describes five bugs as 'four defect groups' plus BUG-005 without stating the grouping. Neither affects runtime behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Align the gate lists and state the grouping explicitly.

limitations: Static review only; no test, lint, verifier or demo run was executed, and no statement here reports an observed run result.

Data files were not supplied (data/cases.json, packet_manifest.json, reviewer_packets/*). Unverified data-specific assumptions: exactly 24 cases and 103 events; every case containing event E1 (assumed by demo_reviews.fixture and the IntakeTests fixture); no case containing E999 or 999+ context items; at least one case having context (test_available_context_reference_is_accepted); the manifest containing the exact substring '"synthetic": true' (test_rejects_duplicate_json_keys); reviewer README contents; whether A and B are actually ordered differently; and whether manifest digests match.
docs/review_protocol.md, the CI workflow, .ai-project.toml and the other linked docs were not supplied, so their claims could not be checked.
Python-version-specific behavior (Path.resolve on symlink loops in 3.11 vs 3.13, fromisoformat leniency, int digit limits) is reasoned from documented stdlib semantics, not observed.
Kappa, the Wilson formula and the demo arithmetic (22/24, kappa 7/8 = 0.875; rotated kappa = -0.5; constant labels give undefined kappa) were checked by hand.
The reproduction and red-test claims in issues.md cannot be confirmed from a static snapshot.
This review gives no semantic judgment of any synthetic case and makes no human-labeling or product-validation claim.
positive_checks: load_submission hashes and parses the same byte snapshot, and ReviewStudy reads cases, manifest and rubric from PacketVerifier's post-verify snapshot. This matches the BUG-006/BUG-007 descriptions; verify() clears and rebuilds the snapshot and also clears it on failure.
Duplicate JSON keys are rejected via object_pairs_hook. The test is meaningful because the manifest is not self-hashed, so without the hook verification would pass.
Exact CSV header, row count and per-row width checks, plus a duplicate-row and full-set check, mean intake never silently drops rows.
Per-row reviewer_id, reviewer_kind and rubric_version must match metadata. Metadata are bound to the manifest digest, rubric digest and responses digest.

agreement() uses exact Fractions. The 0.70 comparison is safe because float rounding is monotonic and 7/10 rounds to the same double as 0.70. The Wilson interval formula is correct, and kappa is null (numeric_gate UNDEFINED) exactly when expected agreement is 1.
human_gate is unconditionally PENDING in every report and CLI result. Nonhuman inputs give INELIGIBLE_NONHUMAN, and self-declared human inputs give only DECLARED_ONLY.
CLI errors emit only the exception type name, and reports do not echo rationale text. The instruction-like-text tests are consistent with this.
Path checks reject absolute paths, '..' escapes and out-of-root symlinks (subject to the race in SLR-09). Reads are bounded at 2 MB.

The demo refuses existing destinations (exists check plus mkdir exist_ok=False), confines in-root output to runs/ using the resolved path, and labels fixtures synthetic, case_author=True and study_material_seen.
The reviewer folder must contain exactly the expected file names, which catches hidden extra files. Template blank checks cover the quoted-newline case through newline-preserving CSV parsing.
Timestamps must be timezone-aware ISO datetimes, and events cannot postdate the cutoff. Null event times are allowed as unknown.
Test counts claimed in TESTING.md (15 original plus 8 packet contracts; 25 review/demo contracts) match the test methods present.
Rubric category and reason-code lists currently match DIMENSIONS and REASONS on static comparison.
